meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did Owen get a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend. So which part of 4.3 says a version history is enough on its own?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. If there's a draft, he'll bring it. Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm reading it. Students misquote plays all the time. And you still haven't told me whether anything is on his record.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. It isn't in the scene. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record, and it stays quiet.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
I'm reading both. Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, before December 1, nothing on his record, and I want it in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. I'll confirm it with Owen and put it in my email tonight, so your written confirmation should name the date.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday the twelfth and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still need that offer in writing with the date named, and I will confirm the date with Owen myself. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted the private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, but she still wants the offer in writing tonight with the date named. That is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You opened the play to Act 3, Scene 2 and told her to search it herself for the quotation, because she could check it with her own eyes.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether anything was on his record unanswered through two of her turns, which kept her pressing it instead of weighing your evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the file created at 11:31 PM the night before the due date and the text arriving at 11:52 and 11:58, came very close to that night, and she covered it by going straight to procedure. It proves nothing about the essay itself, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his record, tell her plainly what is and is not there before you move to your evidence, so that her strongest demand is met early.
